[Heidelberg University](/wiki/Heidelberg_University "Heidelberg University"), Germany's oldest institution of higher learning and generally considered one of its most renowned

Responsibility for educational supervision in Germany is primarily organised within the individual [states](/wiki/States_of_Germany "States of Germany"). Optional [kindergarten](/wiki/Kindergarten "Kindergarten") education is provided for all children between three and six years old, after which [school attendance is compulsory](/wiki/Schulpflicht "Schulpflicht") for at least nine years depending on the state. Primary education usually lasts for four to six years.[[254]](#cite_note-ED-261) Secondary schooling is divided into tracks based on whether students pursue [academic](/wiki/College-preparatory_school "College-preparatory school") or [vocational education](/wiki/Vocational_education "Vocational education").[[255]](#cite_note-262) A system of apprenticeship called *[Duale Ausbildung](/wiki/Dual_education_system "Dual education system")* leads to a skilled qualification which is almost comparable to an academic degree. It allows students in vocational training to learn in a company as well as in a state-run trade school.[[254]](#cite_note-ED-261) This model is well regarded and reproduced all around the world.[[256]](#cite_note-263)

Most of the [German universities](/wiki/List_of_universities_in_Germany "List of universities in Germany") are public institutions, and students traditionally study without fee payment.[[257]](#cite_note-264) The general requirement for attending university is the *[Abitur](/wiki/Abitur "Abitur")*.

Similarities between Yuta and Itadori include their introduction to Jujutsu, experiences with tragedy, naivety, and having faced death.
